fairness.eval_surfaces: dev + test_random (train excluded; test views untouched)
fairness.model_selection: none - one fixed configuration per family

caveats: IN-DISTRIBUTION COMPARISON: 895/1004 gold items come from deterministic template frames, and train/eval share those frames. The TF-IDF numbers are therefore an UPPER BOUND (frame memorisation inflates them), not a field estimate. They show the trained family can learn Nigerian financial phrasing that the lexicon missed, and the gap-vs-lexicon is real — but only fresh, human-confirmed, non-templated labels can bound real-world accuracy. The curated-only rows on the full eval surfaces are the honest signpost, at small n.
Kappa here is agreement between assisted labels and each system, not inter-annotator agreement.

rows.interpretation: positive = the trained model beats the lexicon on held-out assisted labels; a small positive delta does not close the credibility gap (labels are model-assisted, review pending)
